entries.appliesTo: any person using an image of a child under seventeen to train an AI model to produce child sexual abuse materials

sources.prohibition: R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3) — 'It shall also be a violation of this Section for a person to use an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials.'
sources.coveredSubjects: R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3) — 'an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created'

flags: Age threshold is seventeen ('a child under the age of seventeen years') but ai-crimes has no age param in the fixed vocabulary; recorded here rather than as a param.
No fine, imprisonment term, or enforcer appears in the enacted text; penalties presumably live in unamended subsections of R.S. 14:81.1 not reproduced in this act — exposure omitted per rules 3-4.

R.S. 14:81.1(A)(4) removes an element of the existing offense: 'It is not a required element of an offense under this Section that the child depicted in the child sexual abuse materials be a natural person.' (covers wholly AI-generated depictions).
R.S. 14:81.1(G) extends the trier-of-fact age-determination factors to 'the image used to train an artificial intelligence model' — evidentiary provision, fits no listed duty/param.
